title: Retraining a frozen probe unit yields a DIFFERENT checkpoint
status: OBSERVED 2026-10-10 (UTC), on two paid sessions of the same frozen unit
_contract: A fact about D1's behavioural probes that constrains how their evidence may be combined. It changes no frozen protocol value and authorizes nothing; it exists so nobody later pools two artifacts that share an (arm, seed) label and differ in bytes.

the_observation.frozen_unit: d1_screening_q1_s614923639 -- arm q1, seed 614923639, recipe e1_p1_kd_heavy@0.86M

trained_twice.fate: trained in the session that went on to score

the_observation._runtime_difference: 1.3 seconds out of 3654 -- the two trainings did the same work

why: recovery training runs on CUDA in bf16 autocast. Reduction order in GEMMs and atomics is not fixed across launches, so a seeded run is reproducible in distribution and not bit-for-bit. A3 established the same property one level down for the ATTENTION scorer, where batch shape moved a top-k selection.
what_it_does_NOT_mean: it is NOT a defect in the recipe, the seed derivation or the trainer: a recovery seed fixes the data order and the initialization, not the floating-point reduction order
it does NOT invalidate either session. Attempt 103442 produced no measurement at all -- its probe was never scored -- so there is no result to have retried, pooled or selected between
it does NOT make a screening comparison unsound. Every probe a given session scores is trained inside that session, so the five arms are compared to each other under one training execution

what_it_DOES_constrain.never_pool_across_sessions: the preserved checkpoint of 103442 and the probe of 132919 are TWO ARTIFACTS for one (arm, seed) label. A ranking or verdict that mixed one session's probe with another's would compare arms measured under different training executions, which is precisely the pooling the retry policy forbids.
what_it_DOES_constrain.the_preserved_copy_is_unused_evidence: 103442's probe remains evidence that the durability mechanism works, and insurance. It is NOT an input to any measurement and must not become one.
what_it_DOES_constrain.restore_rather_than_retrain_next_time: 103442's closeout chose to retrain rather than restore, on transport cost: ~53 minutes to upload 2.38 GiB at the measured ~0.72 MB/s against ~61 minutes to retrain. On cost that reasoning was right and the saving was ~8 minutes. THIS OBSERVATION IS THE ARGUMENT AGAINST IT: P8.4 state 2 says 'restore the existing checkpoint and resume at scoring. Do not retrain it', and the reason is visible here -- retraining does not recreate the unit, it creates a second one. If a future session fails after training probes, RESTORE. The marginal minutes are not worth a second artifact under one label.
